messages:
Sam: Quick follow-up from today’s all-hands on pricing/quotas 10. We got a few asks to clarify behavior.
Leah: Happy to clarify. Which corner case should we start with?
Carlos: How exactly does the burst pool interact with monthly credits? Example: customer A has 100k credits + 50k burst. They use 120k in month. How is that billed?
Frank: In that case, 100k uses standard hosted units, the 20k overage draws from the 50k burst. If burst exhausted, remaining overage billed at pay-as-you-go rates. No credit roll-forward.
Mira: If a customer is on Dedicated + Hosted credits, which units are consumed first when they call the hosted API?
Leah: Order of consumption: reserved/dedicated commitments (if the request is routed to dedicated capacity and tagged), then hosted credits, then burst, then pay-as-you-go. Well add explicit examples in the billing docs.
DevX Jen: Can customers see a live breakdown in Console? Weve had requests for a timeline view showing credits burned vs burst used.
Leah: Console will show a per-day chart and an API endpoint for programmatic queries (/v1/usage/balance). Beta next sprint.
Carlos: About rate limits: you mentioned soft per-route quotas with auto-fallback. What happens to in-flight requests when fallback triggers?
Frank: In-flight requests continue to completion on the original route. New requests are routed to fallback models once the soft quota threshold plus configured cooldown is hit.
Sam: Are fallbacks configurable per-route and per-org?
Leah: Yes. Admins can set route-level fallback chains and the soft/hard thresholds. Well provide JSON policy snippets in the docs.
Carlos: What about retries? If a client retries after receiving a 429, do those units count again?
Frank: Retries count as normal units. For high-volume clients, recommend idempotency tokens and exponential backoff. Were exploring a retry-window de-dup feature for identical requests to reduce double-billing.
Mira: For enterprise customers who opt into strict pinning (no fallback), do we provide capacity guarantees or a paid surge option?
Leah: Yes. Enterprise can buy reserved windows and guaranteed slots. If they select strict pinned behavior, requests will fail when capacity is lacking unless they also purchase surge capacity.
DevX Jen: Can we get a short sample policy to paste into onboarding docs?
Leah: Example snippet: 
````
{
  "route": "/generate",
  "soft_quota_per_month": "500000",
  "hard_quota_per_month": "600000",
  "fallback_chain": ["gpt-lite-quant", "gpt-compat-embed"],
  "alert_to": "#oncall-ops"
}
````
Carlos: Nice. Also, how do marketplace credits interact with our monthly credits? Are they additive?
Frank: Marketplace credits are applied after hosted credits but before burst and pay-as-you-go. Well add a priority table in the billing FAQ.
Sam: Action items: Leah publish the /v1/usage API spec and Console mockups; Frank document retry billing + de-dupe research; DevX Jen prepare policy snippets and put them in the docs PR.
ops-bot: Tasks assigned: Leah -> /v1/usage API spec (due 2026-04-01). Frank -> retry-billing + de-dupe writeup (due 2026-04-05). DevX Jen -> docs PR with policy snippets (due 2026-03-30).
Mira: Thanks for walking through, much clearer now.
Sam: If anyone has edge cases around grants, multi-org billing, or partner credits DM me.
Leah: Ill post a 5-bullet FAQ in #all-hands summarizing the changes and links to the docs.
Sam: Closing thread 10. Thanks everyone!
